messages:
anya: follow-up from today's arch sync  proposing "compact-on-evict" hybrid: instead of immediate free for tiny async-offloaded items, try opportunistic in-place compaction on the eviction path to reduce scatter and avoid hot compaction cycles.

paul: quick summary: when evicting small items (kvcache entries / tiny embeddings) we attempt to fill the freed slot from nearby inbound allocations in the same page/superblock before publishing free to global freelist. If fill fails, fall back to normal free. The idea is to bias locality without a heavy background mover.

devon: interesting. that trades cost to the evict path for less background compaction. what about tail latency impact on eviction-critical paths?

anya: agree; plan is a bounded best-effort attempt: try up to N candidate moves (N=2) and limit CPU work per-evict to M microseconds (e.g., 200us). If budget exhausted, we drop to normal free and increment a telemetry counter.

sam: how do we pick candidates to move into the hole? we don't want to scan long lists.

anya: use per-superblock short LRU lists of recently-allocated slots. On free, sample LRU head and attempt atomic slot copy+CAS into hole. We only consider slots that are same-size-class and resident (not in-flight).

paul: race cases: concurrent alloc/evict on the same superblock, and device DMA moving blocks between host/device. need careful ordering to avoid copying stale pointers.

devon: propose per-slot state bits: PENDING_MOVE, LIVE, FREED. move is a three-step: mark source PENDING_MOVE (CAS), copy payload to hole, publish target as LIVE, then CAS source to FREED. If any step fails, rollback and let evict fallback.

frag-bot: perf note: prototype run alpha_compact_3 => fragmentation -9%, compaction_cycles -24%, p95 +3.5ms on evict path under steady chat+embed mix.

sam: those numbers are promising. still worried about worst-case: if many moves fail we waste CPU. we should only attempt moves when node CPU is below threshold.

anya: agreed. add cheap throttles: node-level trylock, per-thread local budget token, and skip logic when CPU pressure signal from kernel > 70%.

paul: device interplay: when superblock contents live on device, move needs to touch staging buffers and possibly trigger PCIe memcpy. that's expensive. how do we handle host<->device residency?

anya: heuristic: only attempt compact-on-evict when allocation residency == host or when we can complete device memcpy in a batched window (e.g., we aggregate multiple move-copies and issue a single device memcpy). If item is pinned on-device (hot-token), skip and rely on token system.

devon: batching device moves makes sense. we can accumulate up to K moves per-superblock then issue an async batch memcpy to GPU. That keeps PCIe efficiency. Need to ensure correct ordering with other IO.

sam: telemetry wishlist: evict_attempts, moves_success, moves_fail_reason, avg_move_latency, device_move_batch_size, cpu_throttle_hits. Also a breakdown of compaction cycles avoided.

anya: rollout plan:
- alpha: runtime flag behind dev clusters, compact-on-evict limited to host-resident tiny-objects and N=1 candidate
- beta: enable batching for device moves on testpool, add per-node throttles and console metrics
- gamma: per-tenant knobs + integrate with lease/token budgets and eviction escalation rules

paul: test plan: mixed workload with 100k tiny keys churn, steady chat streams, and a malicious tenant that allocates pinned small keys. measure fragmentation ratio, compaction cycles/sec, p95/p99 latency on both alloc and evict paths, and device memcpy qps.

devon: add failure semantics doc: if move fails after payload copy, we must not leak a live duplicate. implement idempotent retries and a reclamation tombstone with monotonic sequence id for replay.

frag-bot: bench queued: `compact_on_evict_bench --id=coev_9909 --runs=10 --pattern=mixed_spike` on benchpool-4.

sam: small UX question: should we expose this to Dedicated customers as an opt-in? some may want deterministic evict latencies.

anya: yes opt-in. default off for Hosted initially. Dedicated can enable in beta with console slider for aggressiveness.

paul: fine. please put a 2-page concise RFC in the arch repo + short design diagram and a checklist for infra (CPU budget knob, bench nodes).

anya: will do. thanks all, will post bench results in 48h.

devon: I'll review code once prototype lands.

frag-bot: job scheduled: `compact_on_evict_bench --ref=coev_9909 --notify=#eng-runtime`
